prompt_version: s5-extract-facts-v2 (adapted from Paleo Atlas extract-facts-v3; v2 after Sofía's S5 review)

facts.statement: Participants were asked to recall, suppress, or simply look at cues associated with unpleasant memories.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Brain activity was measured using electroencephalography (EEG) while the participants performed the task.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: People with insomnia showed weaker memory control, indicated by less forgetting of memories they were told to suppress compared to the healthy group.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: During the suppression phase, the insomnia group had higher P300 brain signals, which are a known marker of conscious memory retrieval.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: This brain signal suggests that people with insomnia continued to unconsciously retrieve the memories even when trying to suppress them.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The healthy group did not show this difference in brain signals, suggesting they successfully blocked the memory traces.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that future studies are needed to determine if memory control deficits cause insomnia symptoms or are just associated with them.
facts.subject: humans
